prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on your goals (social short-form vs. long-form, e‑commerce vs. brand spot), budget, need for real-looking presenters or stylized generated visuals, and how much control you want. That said, here are the top options by use case, with the strengths and trade-offs to help you choose.

Top picks (by use case)

- Best for AI presenters / corporate-style ads: Synthesia
  - Why: High-quality, realistic AI avatars and multiple languages, easy script → video workflow, good branding controls.
  - Pros: Fast, polished results; no actors/shooting; enterprise features.
  - Cons: Cost scales for enterprise; less creative/stylized control than raw editing tools.

- Best for short-form social ads & templates: Canva (Video) or InVideo
  - Why: Huge template libraries for Instagram/FB/TikTok/Reels, drag‑and‑drop editing, simple AI text-to-video tools.
  - Pros: Fast, affordable, great for teams and brand kits.
  - Cons: Not for advanced generative visuals or hyper-real avatars.

- Best for repurposing articles/scripts → videos: Pictory
  - Why: Converts long-form text into short videos automatically with captions and stock clips.
  - Pros: Saves time on repurposing content; good captioning and voiceover options.
  - Cons: Less creative control; stock footage look.

- Best for advanced creative / generative visuals: Runway (Gen-2) or Kaiber
  - Why: Cutting‑edge image/video generation and effects for unique, cinematic ads.
  - Pros: Highly creative, can produce visuals you can’t shoot easily.
  - Cons: Learning curve, longer render times, more experimental.

- Best for quick product/e‑commerce ads: Promo.com
  - Why: Ad-focused templates, product promo flows, integrated stock footage and music.
  - Pros: Marketing-focused, optimized durations and CTAs.
  - Cons: Template look unless customized.

- Best for easy editing + AI voiceovers/transcripts: Descript
  - Why: Overdub custom voices, text-based video editing, great for quick voiceovers and edits.
  - Pros: Precise editing, natural-sounding synthetic voices.
  - Cons: Not templated; you still build the ad timeline.

- Best for all-around editing + collaborative workflow: VEED / Kapwing
  - Why: Good mix of AI features (subtitles, text-to-speech, text-to-video), quick social export presets.
  - Pros: Easy collaboration, web-based editing.
  - Cons: Quality depends on inputs; less advanced avatar capabilities.

- Best low-cost / fastest free option: Biteable or Clipchamp
  - Why: Very simple templates and quick output, free tiers for basic needs.
  - Pros: Fast, cheap.
  - Cons: Template-y look, watermark on some free plans.

How to pick the best one for you
1. Define your priority: realistic presenter, templated social ads, generative visuals, or repurposing content.
2. Consider budget: enterprise AI presenters (Synthesia/HeyGen) cost more than Canva/InVideo.
3. Test 2–3 tools: most offer free trials or freemium tiers — try your typical script and format.
4. Check exports & formats: aspect ratios for ads (9:16 for Reels/TikTok, 1:1/16:9), bitrate, branding export (brand kit, fonts).
5. Look at integrations: ad platforms, Shopify, analytics, or team collaboration features you need.

If you tell me: (a) your budget, (b) target platform(s) and ad length, and (c) whether you need a real-looking presenter vs. stylized visuals, I’ll recommend the 1–2 best tools and a suggested workflow.
